method: SG042 HAC lag-3 SE on 24 ten-sample medians, OLS slope per observation, original nominal 90% z=1.645; split-calibration 90th percentile of |estimate-known_synthetic_slope|/SE, empirical rank ceil((360+1)*.90)=325; fixed240 data and independent decision gate.

holdout.full_miscoverage_ledger: Generated deterministically by committed Python executable; locally generated full report /mnt/data/sg043/holdout.json

findings: SG042 original nominal 90% intervals covered true programmed slopes in only 554/720 (76.94%) holdout traces
Split-calibrated correction covered 636/720 (88.33%), below 90% sample target
Conditional coverage fell to 62/80 (77.5%) in colored-noise group, 66/80 (82.5%) correlation-switch group
Corrected interval reduced incorrect decisions 89 to 42 at cost of raising abstentions 25 to 101
This is fixed240 interval-only decision rule, not direct SG042 end-to-end controller comparison
limitations: Split-conformal quantile provides a marginal statement only under exchangeability between calibration and test standardized residuals; synthetic group dependencies or shifts may break it
Observed 88.33% rather than exact 90% not alone a formal significance rejection of nominal coverage
The rule prefers confirmed when CI excludes zero, and rejected only when equivalence CI lies within ±0.0032; ambiguity withheld
Truth labels are known because streams are synthetic; not a real-world data-source validation
SE and standardized errors are computed on all 240 continuation samples, no early stopping optimization
Same design family used across calibration/holdout but seeds did not overlap

retrieval_log.result: 636 intervals covered, 84 misses; corrected decision cost 18426 vs original 24048
